statements.quote: A custom-designed ideation tool, developed specifically for the study (Appendix 1), was employed to compare traditional and GenAI-augmented brainstorming techniques.
statements.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), Section 4.1, opening sentence; reference to included Appendix 1.

statements.quote: Study participants logged in with unique codes to ensure proper group assignment, anonymity, and secure data storage.
statements.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), Section 4.1, first paragraph.

statements.quote: When a team member posed a problem, the tool's advanced algorithm broke it down into components, converting them into detailed queries for the GPT-4 backend (Appendix 1). For each problem, the system generated four AI personas, each with specialized expertise, tailored to the problem at hand to maximize output quality. These personas engaged dynamically in brainstorming sessions, offering insights and feedback like human experts (Appendix 1). Teams could regenerate personas with refined problem descriptions in a separate tab, enabling a flexible brainstorming process.
statements.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), Section 4.1, second paragraph; references to Appendix 1.

statements.quote: The tool’s backend architecture featured a database interface that recorded every user interaction, idea, and solution proposal in real-time, ensuring no loss of data and providing a complete record for analysis. For task management, the tool allowed teams to display, discuss, and input solutions directly within the interface, with solutions only saved once consensus was reached, promoting collaborative decision-making. Additionally, the tool employed an automated prompt sequencing system, continuously feeding the ongoing conversation transcript into the AI to prevent repetitive outputs and ensure each contribution was unique and contextually relevant.
statements.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), Section 4.1, database and prompt-sequencing paragraph.

statements.quote: Additionally, to ensure unbiased evaluation, ideas generated by both groups were anonymized and combined into a curated database, preventing any traceability to the original teams by the expert jury.
statements.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), Section 4.1, curated idea database.

statements.quote: Participants, unaware of their group assignment, completed identical tasks using the same background information.
statements.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), Section 4.1, final paragraph.

statements.quote: The control group began brainstorming after a brief introduction, with their task completion time recorded. The experimental group had an introduction and Q&A session about the AI tool, followed by access to the GenAI-supported platform, which logged inputs, completion times, and individual contributions. Both groups followed a 45-minute maximum task duration but could submit earlier if completed.
statements.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), Section 4.1, experimental procedure and logged data.

statements.quote: For ethical reasons, all inputs were stored anonymously, with unique acronyms assigned to users. Participants provided informed consent and could withdraw from the study at any time.
statements.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), Section 4.1, anonymity and consent paragraph.

statements.quote: Data collection in the experimental group was facilitated through the specialized ideation tool, while the control group used Google Forms. An expert panel evaluated the quality of ideas using Microsoft Forms on a 7-point Likert scale, categorizing them using the Abernathy and Clark (1985) innovation matrix [82]. Variables such as idea quality based on Dean et al. (2006) [20], processing times, and the evaluation criteria were rigorously operationalized and validated through usability tests, pilot studies, and calibration exercises.
statements.locator: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 13), Section 4.2, first prose paragraph.

statements.quote: For the analysis, the Phyton based Data Science platform Anaconda 3 and Jupyter Notebooks were utilized to ensure an efficient and effective evaluation of the data.
statements.locator: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 13), Section 5, opening sentence; Phyton is the source spelling.

statements.quote: The consistent results across both tasks justified combining the datasets to strengthen the analysis.
statements.locator: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 13), Section 5, final sentence.

deposits.notes:
DataCite title and first-author searches independently confirmed the Mendeley DOI lead in candidates.json. The deposit explicitly says it accompanies this paper by Michael Gindert and Marvin Lutz Müller. The paper and form do not name the deposit. Published 2024-11-12; versions API lists only version 1. The concept DOI 10.17632/5vcxb928rz and version DOI 10.17632/5vcxb928rz.1 identify one deposit, counted once.

The closest permitted contents label is aggregate_only: these are scores aggregated at the team-idea level, with one row per team proposal, rather than participant records. Individual idea rows are retained; this is richer than arm-level summary tables. There is no permitted output_level_without_participant_id label. Idea Nr. is an idea identifier, not a participant or team identifier.

All three Excel workbooks were downloaded without credentials and read completely in memory. No workbook has additional sheets, hidden rows, hidden columns, merged cells, or formulas. Combined_matrix.xlsx contains Idee 1 through Idee 48. Task1_matrix.xlsx contains Idee 1 through Idee 24; Task2_matrix.xlsx contains Idee 25 through Idee 48. The combined data rows exactly concatenate the two task files; there are 48 distinct output records, not 96. Each task has 12 IsExperiment=0 and 12 IsExperiment=1 rows; the combined file has 24 per arm. No data cells are missing.

IsExperiment=0 denotes control/no AI and IsExperiment=1 denotes the experimental GenAI arm: the observed combined aggregate-score means are 3.5462962954166666 and 4.583333333333333 respectively, matching the paper's control 3.546 and experimental 4.583 (PDF pp. 16-17, Section 5). The ten score columns cover S1-O1 through S1-O10. Has_arm_assignment refers to each idea's arm; individual randomization records are absent.

columns_checked is the union of observed headers: Combined_matrix.xlsx and Task1_matrix.xlsx use Paradigm relatedness and Implicational explicitness; Task2_matrix.xlsx uses Paradigm_relatedness and Implicational_explicitness. All other headers match. Each workbook has 12 columns.

No participant IDs, team membership, team sizes, or reliable cross-task team identifier/crosswalk are included. Pairing task rows by a 24-idea offset contradicts the arm labels in 8 of the 24 possible pairs, so that mapping must not be inferred. The dataset description repeats n=70 and teams of three but does not document distinct people represented in the analyzed rows. The final analyzed people count remains unconfirmed.

There are no proposal texts, individual contributions, conversation transcripts, innovation-type classifications (S1-O11 through S1-O14), time measurements, satisfaction responses, rater-level records, analysis notebooks/code, README, or codebook among the deposited files. The landing-page description mentions time, diversity and satisfaction results, but the actual files contain only idea identifiers, arm indicators and ten quality scores.

Aggregated equals the unweighted mean of the nine component score columns within 0.00000001 for every deposited row. This is an empirical reconstruction from rounded stored values; the workbooks contain no formula cells or documentation establishing the authors' original aggregation code, standardizer, bootstrap unit or error-bar definition.

File inventory verified with https://data.mendeley.com/public-api/datasets/5vcxb928rz/files?folder_id=root&version=1 (HTTP 200, three files) and explicit $start=0&$limit=1000 (HTTP 200, same three files). https://data.mendeley.com/public-api/datasets/5vcxb928rz/folders/1 returned HTTP 200 and an empty list. https://data.mendeley.com/public-api/datasets/5vcxb928rz/versions returned HTTP 200 with version 1 available. https://doi.org/10.17632/5vcxb928rz.1 and https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/5vcxb928rz both returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to the version-1 landing page. https://api.datacite.org/dois/10.17632/5vcxb928rz.1 returned HTTP 200 and confirmed open-access metadata and the license.

Exploratory Mendeley routes /public-api/datasets/5vcxb928rz/versions/1 and /public-api/datasets/5vcxb928rz/folders?version=1 returned HTTP 404; these were incorrect API routes, not dead deposit links. /api/docs returned HTTP 200 but only a JavaScript shell. The publicly served /datasets/bundle.js?5e5376ee3a5def54f781 returned HTTP 200 and supplied the correct anonymous folders, versions and paginated files endpoints. No login or access request was needed.

what_we_could_compute: For final.open_items[2], calculate arm-specific means, sample SDs, and output counts for S1-O1 through S1-O10 from the 48 idea records, either combined or separately for the two tasks. Task-specific team-output SEs and confidence intervals can be calculated using 12 team proposals per arm; these are not per-person statistics.

For final.open_items[2] and [4], calculate numerical Cohen's d from the deposited rounded scores with an explicitly chosen standardizer, such as the pooled sample SD. This permits numerical comparison with Figure 5 but does not prove which standardizer the authors used or resolve their intended prose/figure interpretation.

For final.open_items[2], empirically reconstruct the stored aggregate score as the unweighted mean of the nine component columns, matching every row within 0.00000001. Original analysis code, definitive formula documentation and Figure 3 error-bar definitions remain unavailable.

For final.open_items[1], the public files do not link a team's outputs across tasks. Combined-output descriptive SDs can be computed, but valid pooled SEs/CIs accounting for repeated team outputs, team-average effects and the original bootstrap resampling procedure cannot be recovered. Task-specific analyses avoid that cross-task repetition.

Final.open_items[0] remains unresolved: participant-level means, SDs, SEs, allocation counts, actual team sizes, and the distinct final analyzed people count cannot be recovered. The 48 rows count proposals. Final.open_items[3], the setting/context question, also remains unresolved by these spreadsheets.
Text-based idea diversity or homogenization cannot be computed because no texts/ideas are deposited; innovation-category diversity cannot be computed because category labels are also absent.
notes:
The complete 102620-character markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks through the appendices, references, acknowledgements and final declaration. Relevant PDF pages were checked using PyMuPDF text extraction. The 41-page local PDF is byte-for-byte identical to the current https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.18357v4 (HTTP 200; 1402839 bytes), downloaded in memory; arXiv identifies v4 as revised 2025-02-25.

There is no explicit data-sharing, code-sharing, on-request, preregistration, external supplement or repository statement in the paper. statements records relevant data collection/storage, software and included-materials descriptions verbatim, with PDF line wrapping normalized to spaces. Appendix 1 consists of four interface screenshots. The acknowledgements (PDF p. 40) and writing declaration (p. 41) contain no availability statement. No external PDF hyperlink annotations were present, and the only GitHub mentions refer to Copilot/another paper. The form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are empty. Ordinary bibliography links to other works are not this study's deposits.

The preprint landing page https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18357 returned HTTP 200. Its full-text links contain the paper PDF and license, with no study-specific supplementary dataset, external data/code deposit, journal DOI or journal-ref identified. Generic arXiv code/data service toggles are not deposit links.

All network requests used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without an email address, credentials, account creation or access requests. Repository files were read only in memory. Only forms/data/c330.json was written.

Searches: DataCite https://api.datacite.org/dois?query=<query>&page[size]=100 returned HTTP 200 for both the quoted full title (without the parenthetical Preprint) and Gindert. Each returned three records: this preprint and the concept/version DOI records for the same Mendeley deposit. relevant therefore lists one deduplicated deposit.

Harvard Dataverse https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api/search?q=<query>&per_page=100 returned HTTP 200 and zero results for both the quoted full title and Gindert. Zenodo https://zenodo.org/api/records?q=<query>&size=100 initially returned HTTP 400 for each query, explicitly limiting unauthenticated searches to 25 results per page; both were retried anonymously with size=25 and returned HTTP 200, zero results. Failed requests have n_results=null rather than zero.

OSF https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/?filter[title]=<query>&page[size]=100 returned HTTP 200 and total=0 for both the full title and the first-author token Gindert. The Gindert title-filter query is only a literal title search; an additional public author lookup at https://api.osf.io/v2/users/?filter[full_name]=Gindert&page[size]=100 also returned HTTP 200 and total=0. A broader title query ideation timed out after 30 seconds, so its count and relevance are null. The alternative title query Impact of GenAI returned HTTP 200 and three unrelated projects (4keb5: media-subscription disclosure; en3p5: critical-thinking literature review; 6r4zk: graduates' jobs), with no relevant deposit. OSF counts were read from links.meta.total. The alternative query was requested twice; both responses agreed.

High confidence in public_partial is based on complete inspection of all three files and verification of empty repository folders, rather than the landing page's broader claims. The unsuccessful broad OSF query limits exhaustive discovery claims; none_found is not the conclusion. Public participant-level data were not confirmed.
